editorial.headline: Integrated Electricity Supply With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35140 covers end-to-end electricity supply, from generation to final sale, and is nationally open to foreign ownership without a Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35140 is the integrated electricity-supply category: a single business framework for generating power, moving it through transmission and distribution networks, storing it, and selling it to final consumers. Its defining feature is unity of activity. The code is not merely about one isolated part of the electricity chain; it is about operating those linked functions as one business. The scope also expressly includes public electric-vehicle charging stations when they are integrated with generation, bringing charging infrastructure inside the same electricity-supply logic when the power source is part of the setup.

That breadth matters for founders because this is a serious operating category rather than a narrow service label. The record places it open across all business scales: micro, small, medium, and large. In practical editorial terms, the code can describe anything from a smaller integrated operation to a large-scale electricity business, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope of generation, network delivery, storage, and sale to end users. The scope text also names cross-border electricity network interconnection and cross-border electricity sales permits, so the category is written with both domestic integration and cross-border electricity activity in view.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The activity is marked open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the national field: the record allows full foreign ownership at the national level. That is the first anchor for any PMA reading of this code, and it should not be softened into a vague “possibly open” conclusion.

Bali is also open for this code today under the record provided. The province’s moratorium blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide on a permanent basis, but KBLI 35140 is not blocked here: the Bali reason states that OSS risk at large scale is medium-high or high, so it is not caught by that moratorium. The honest national-versus-Bali picture is therefore unusually direct: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule. The Bali status still reads OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, which should be understood as an openness signal tied to a higher-risk OSS profile, not as a hidden ban.
